name: Malchijah
overview: Malchijah was a male Levite belonging to the Gershonite family, specifically identified as the son of Ethni. His lineage places him within the tribe of Levi, known for their priestly duties and service in the tabernacle. The designation as a Gershonite connects him to Gershon, a son of Levi, highlighting his role within this particular Levitical branch.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchijah means 'y-h-v-h is [my] king,' reflecting a theologically rich declaration of God's sovereignty. This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 6:40, underscores the believer’s recognition of the Lord as sovereign King, though it was not explicitly given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Malchijah as the son of Ethni and infers Baaseiah as his father, situating him within a specific Levitical family line. These relationships provide a clear genealogical context within the tribe of Levi as recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:40-41.
scriptureSignificance: Malchijah's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, which affirm the continuity of priestly service through the generations. His identification as a Gershonite son of Ethni roots him firmly in the Levitical tradition, emphasizing the faithfulness of God's appointed servants. By tracing this lineage, Scripture highlights the preservation of God's covenantal order through the tribe of Levi.
